slogan: Where Atomic Settlement Meets Liquidity Efficiency

problem.title: Why do we need NettedX?
problem.lead: Traditional settlement is not broken because value is missing. It is expensive because gross obligations keep accumulating, and each movement of value demands fresh liquidity.
problem.conclusion: The problem isn't the amount of value being moved. It's how much liquidity must be committed to move it.

aggregate.title: {highlight} · Trade Intake
aggregate.text: The system continuously accepts and aggregates pending obligations. No assets move during this window; only the netting intent is recorded on-chain.

freeze.title: {highlight} · Window Closed & Netting
freeze.text: Starting from block 11, new transactions enter the next settlement window. The smart contract then calculates and notifies each participant’s net position based on the fixed transaction set, ensuring stable obligations during settlement.

waiting.title: {highlight} · Funding Wait
waiting.text: This period are reserved for funding verification, risk checks, and final readiness confirmation. Assets remain under each participant's control while the protocol waits for completion.

settle.title: {highlight} · Settlement
settle.text: In Block 14, the network executes the final netting and atomic settlement. All receivables and payables are cleared in the same transaction, with all-or-nothing execution guaranteed.

beforeAfter.desc: NettedX turns gross obligations into net settlement.
beforeAfter.footer: Based on an assumption of 1000 transactions, the efficiency of NettedX is calculated.

howWorks.title: How It Works
howWorks.desc: With the help of cutting-edge technologies, we continue to innovate.

card1.title: Smart Contract
card1.desc: We use smart contracts to record transaction obligations, verify netting results, and execute atomic asset transfers, ensuring that settlement either completes entirely or reverts as a whole.

card2.title: On-chain Netting Engine
card2.desc: Transactions are aggregated within fixed netting windows, allowing NettedX to calculate each participant’s net position and compress thousands of bilateral obligations into fewer settlement obligations.

card3.title: Atomic Settlement
card3.desc: All netted asset transfers are executed within a single transaction, providing atomicity across participants and eliminating the risk of partial settlement.

card4.title: Liquidity Optimization
card4.desc: By offsetting mutual payment obligations between participants, NettedX reduces the liquidity required to settle the same transaction volume, enabling capital to support more activity.

card5.title: Netting Windows
card5.desc: Transactions are accumulated within a defined block-based window before settlement. During the window, no assets are moved—the protocol only records settlement obligations.

card6.title: Verifiable Settlement
card6.desc: Settlement results can be independently verified on-chain by authorized participants, providing a tamper-resistant record of netting and settlement while reducing reliance on centralized clearing infrastructure.

card7.desc: Net positions are calculated separately for the cash leg and the securities leg, then settled together in a single transaction. Neither side can complete without the other.
card7.title: Cross-Asset Netting

card8.title: Composable Architecture
card8.desc: NettedX provides modular netting and settlement infrastructure that can integrate with existing IT system, protocols, and asset systems.

title.text: Ready to Move More With Less?

features.desc: NettedX provides robust fault tolerance mechanisms.

option1.desc: When a participant is short at settlement, the buffer lends them the difference — inside the same transaction. The system detects the shortfall and covers it in one atomic execution, drawing on a facility the participant set up in advance. Nobody has to predict the shortfall or click anything at the cutoff.

option2.desc: Before settling, the contract checks every net payer's balance and authorisation. Anyone who cannot perform is excluded, positions are recomputed for the rest, and this repeats until the remaining set is viable. Excluded trades roll into the next window and net against new trades.

useCases.desc: Wherever value moves in both directions, netting creates efficiency.

case1.title: Cross-Border Payments
case1.desc: Net bilateral payment obligations across currencies and counterparties to reduce trapped liquidity and improve settlement efficiency.

case2.title: Institutional Settlement
case2.desc: Compress high-volume trading obligations between institutions into fewer net positions, reducing the capital required for settlement.

case3.title: On-chain Settlement
case3.desc: Aggregate recurring on-chain obligations across protocols and users before final settlement, reducing unnecessary asset movement on-chain.

case4.title: Treasury Management
case4.desc: Reduce idle settlement capital by offsetting incoming and outgoing obligations before funds need to move.
